problem: Prior map-based semantic navigation (SemExp, PONI, VLFM, BSC-Nav) uses explicit or structured memory but does not learn to predict how the map will evolve or jointly predict waypoint plans in a shared latent space.
motivation: Agents should anticipate the evolution of observed spatial memory under goal-directed motion, not just retrieve past observations. Latent (JEPA-style) prediction avoids pixel reconstruction, and cognitive-map accounts link predictive spatial memory to flexible planning.
key_idea: Train a goal-conditioned latent world model (Qwen3.5-0.8B backbone) that jointly predicts future map-token features and robot-centric waypoint latents from historical global-memory map tokens, goal and pose, and embed it in a full navigation system.
insight: The paper reports only a single SR/SPL comparison against a reproduced BSC-Nav baseline. SR rises much more than SPL (+8.39 vs +0.65 pts), suggesting better target-search reliability but not clearly shorter paths. No ablations are provided (deferred to a later version), so the contribution of future-map prediction versus waypoint prediction is not isolated.
method: Perception/retrieval/verification: encodes RGB-D into latent features, projects them to the global map, retrieves goal-relevant memory and verifies the target; navigates directly if verified, otherwise triggers predictive exploration.
Spatiotemporal memory: sparse memory combining landmark memory and graph-voxel memory, with add/fuse/refresh updates from real observations only.

GLaM backbone: Qwen3.5-0.8B takes historical map tokens (voxel-fused features from four RGB-D views, 3D RoPE, 2560-d), goal and pose, plus learnable visual and waypoint queries, and outputs future map tokens and waypoint latents in one forward pass.
Waypoint latent codec: MLP encoder maps (dx, dy, sin dtheta, cos dtheta) to 2560-d and a decoder reconstructs it; pretrained via MSE, then frozen for supervision and decoding.
Loss: masked MSE on future-map features plus masked MSE on waypoint latents, weighted by lambda_v and lambda_w; no cross-entropy term.
Data: replay of HM3D ObjectNav expert trajectories (577 episodes, 145 scenes, 55,392 steps) sliced into 12,101 multi-timescale samples.
Planning expert and controller: grounds the decoded waypoint into a feasible subgoal on the observed map and executes it with geometric, collision-aware control.

setting.backbone: Qwen3.5-0.8B (fine-tuned as latent world model) with frozen visual encoder and frozen waypoint encoder/decoder; system relies on BSC-Nav-style memory
setting.training_data: 577 HM3D v0.2 ObjectNav expert episodes over 145 scenes (55,392 steps, ~15.4 h), 12,101 multi-timescale samples
setting.observation: RGB-D (four views for map tokens) + robot pose
setting.action_space: decoded robot-centric waypoint increments executed by a geometric low-level controller
setting.privileged: none stated (no pre-built map or target coordinates); GT pose implied in simulation

numbers.eval_set_note: 50% subset of the HM3D ObjectNav benchmark, same episodes as reproduced BSC-Nav; split not stated explicitly, assumed validation
numbers.extra: compared only to reproduced BSC-Nav (SR 78.50, SPL 47.70) on the same subset
numbers.evidence: Table 1: HM3D-ObjectNav results on the 50% subset reproduction setting

numbers_note: Only one table; the split (validation) is not explicitly named. No ablations reported.
results: On a 50% HM3D-ObjectNav subset, GLAM reaches SR 86.89% and SPL 48.35%, vs the reproduced BSC-Nav at 78.50% and 47.70% (+8.39 SR, +0.65 SPL). Qualitative real-world demos on an Astribot S1 show online exploration and memory retrieval.
limitations: Evaluated only on a 50% subset against a single reproduced baseline; no ablations, no full-benchmark comparison, and no quantitative real-world results.
Trained on expert trajectories only, with deterministic latent predictions and no uncertainty modeling; not an action-conditioned simulator.
Bounded token memory (truncation) and sensitivity to localization drift and larger environments are untested.
